question: Should ClawHub sign the existing stored hosted-feed contract, and what exact trust-root, schema-version, rotation, and failure behavior should the OpenClaw consumer support?
rationale: The answer defines a production signing-secret boundary and what catalog bytes clients authenticate; current repository intent explicitly leaves that decision separate from the unsigned feed implementation.

options.title: Sign Stored Publications
options.body: Wrap the existing immutable, integrity-bound publication bytes and preserve the current route, validators, sequence, and stale-serving behavior.

options.title: Approve A New Contract
options.body: Adopt a separately versioned signed feed only after explicit producer-consumer compatibility, migration, and operations approval.

options.title: Pause Signing
options.body: Keep signing unmerged until key custody, trusted-root delivery, rotation, revocation, and rollout ownership are ready together.

recommendation.title: Sign Stored Publications
recommendation.body: Wrap the existing immutable, integrity-bound publication bytes and preserve the current route, validators, sequence, and stale-serving behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They established the current hosted-feed contract and explicitly separated signing as a later production decision.
